scope: Unified typed browser control checkpoint: Client, Conversation, Participant, Session and Operation; six ordinary mutations, invitation decisions and original-operation recovery over actual local WT and bounded WSS fallback. No Connection/Stream composition, capture/render/UI, real media permission/screen, Linux/remote or complete Gate 6 acceptance claim.

actual_browser.mutation_observation: Fixture forwards original production BrowserClient.request calls unchanged and counts their original operation_id. Exactly sixteen distinct mutation calls (eight per path); wait, status, restore and reconnect do not resend mutations.

implemented: Transport-independent typed control handles, shared nominal ID/revision brands in a runtime-free leaf, invariant typed operation references and SDK-owned result decoders. Node runtime JS remains byte-identical to the base commit; both Node/browser type graphs compile together.

Conversation creation, current Participant lookup, Session invite/accept/reject/cancel/end return observable Operations. Original IDs are supplied by persisted application intent; no implicit mutation waits, replacement IDs, reconnect or retry.

Operation status/wait/waitUntilReady have a finite original read budget, original logical key, immutable reference JSON, record/revision fencing and current authority. Cancelled waits do not cancel mutations. Unsupported continuation and mismatched result/scope refuse. Malformed submitted responses retain uncertain original operation key.

Incoming signed hints yield a scoped Session only after a finite consistent current-authorized snapshot confirms actor Identity, active membership/epoch, live Conversation/Session and invited appearance. Foreign reply/Connection/revision scopes refuse. Single-reader and bounded queue/wait, close and abort never send decisions.

Browser SDK connect/reconnect and operation failures expose canonical typed errors with submission certainty and original keys rather than raw response bodies. Historical receipt snapshots grant no present authority.
behavior: 18 signed browser-boundary tests cover both physical adapters, typed status/restore without resend, incoming scoped accept/reject, malformed original acknowledgement certainty, invariant original references, rollback/rebinding, cancelled read waits, snapshot revision split, foreign completed result, removed/revoked current authorization and invalid incoming scope/overlapping/closed wait.

Owned Chrome runs the same two-actor public typed workflow over direct WT and a 350ms owned UDP-blackhole WT opening followed by WSS with its separately approved profile. Each creates a Conversation, discovers recipient Participant, receives/rejects invitation, explicitly retries a fresh saved Session/operation and accepts, ends, reconnects and restores the original end receipt; then receives and cancels a third invitation. Recipient uses only supplied incoming Session handles, without copied IDs.

After both workflows, each currently selected caller profile is independently revoked. Original status refuses, and explicit reconnect refuses the original enrollment claim. Revoked preferred credential does not cause a fallback. Exactly four credentials/keys, two Devices and four Endpoints persist through status/reconnect/repeated original claims.
